head: Qué va delante
Ejemplo
Efecto
rows: Tired as she was, she kept working.
In the corner stood an old piano.
So great was the noise that nobody slept.
Such was his anger that he left the room.

blocks.title: La inversión después de un lugar
blocks.text: Con un complemento de lugar al principio, el inglés puede poner el verbo delante del sujeto, como el español: En el rincón había un piano = In the corner stood a piano. Pero solo con verbos como be, stand, lie, come y go, y el sujeto no puede ser un pronombre: Here comes the bus, pero Here it comes. Fuera de estos casos, el sujeto va siempre delante.

head: Inglés
Lo que se omite
rows: I'd like to help, but I can't.
She said she would call, and she did.
Have you finished? — Yes, I have.
I didn't want to go, but I had to.
Tom likes jazz and Anna classical music.

blocks.title: to se queda
blocks.text: En la elipsis después de want, would like, have, try, need se mantiene to: You can come if you want to. El español lo omite: si quieres.

head: Palabra
Ejemplo
Español
rows: Is it going to rain? — I think so.
Is he coming? — I hope not.
He was asked to leave, and he did so.
I don't like the red shirt; I prefer the blue one.
Tom and Ben are brothers; the former is a doctor.
el primero / el segundo, este / aquel

blocks.title: Creo que sí = I think so
blocks.text: Creo que sí = I think so, creo que no = I don't think so (o, formal, I think not), espero que sí = I hope so, espero que no = I hope not. Nunca I think yes ni I think that yes. Y el español omite el sustantivo (prefiero la azul), pero el inglés necesita one: I prefer the blue one.

rows: Will she come? — I think yes.
Will she come? — I think so.
Creo que sí = I think so.
Is it serious? — I hope no.
Is it serious? — I hope not.
Espero que no = I hope not.
You can come if you want.
You can come if you want to.
Con un pronombre no hay inversión.
Although tired as she was, she worked.
Tired as she was, she worked.
although y as no van juntos.

blocks.text: Completa con la palabra que falta. Las respuestas están en la última página.

items.q: Is the shop open on Sunday? — I think ______.
items.full: Is the shop open on Sunday? — I think so.

items.q: Will it rain tomorrow? — I hope ______.
items.full: Will it rain tomorrow? — I hope not.

items.q: ______ as he was, he still finished the race.
items.full: Tired as he was, he still finished the race.

items.q: So loud ______ the music that we couldn't talk.
items.full: So loud was the music that we couldn't talk.

items.q: In the middle of the room ______ a large table.
items.full: In the middle of the room stood a large table.

items.q: I wanted to call her, but I didn't have time ______.
items.full: I wanted to call her, but I didn't have time to.

items.q: These shoes are too small. Have you got bigger ______?
items.full: These shoes are too small. Have you got bigger ones?

items.q: He promised to apologise, and he did ______.
items.full: He promised to apologise, and he did so.

items.q: Such ______ the demand that tickets sold out in an hour.
items.full: Such was the demand that tickets sold out in an hour.

items.q: Have you seen the film? — Yes, I ______.
items.full: Have you seen the film? — Yes, I have.

items.q: En el rincón había un piano viejo.
items.a: In the corner stood an old piano.
You can come if you want to.
